input.summary:
Cottage bedroom furnished in parts/room-34.mjs: red bed on the west wall as focal piece, barrel nightstand with flower pot, fence-and-top-slab table with two stair chairs and a candle, chest dresser in the SE corner, two hanging lanterns.
Built with make.sh (12 blocks placed, no REFUSED or off-palette lines); the room tool reports min light 11, 0 dark cells, and the lane from the door at x80 z71 is clear.
Walk verdict is UNREACHABLE only because the parlour and shell are still stubs in this copy; the lanterns float until the cottage plate at y6 exists.
left: WALK not verified: the room check says 0 of 7 floor cells reachable because the door's parlour side and the cottage floor/plate are still stubs in this copy; re-run $MCD room once the shell and outbuildings parts are merged.
Two hanging lanterns at (79,5,72) and (80,5,74) show as floating until the cottage plate at y6 is built (outbuildings part).
Floor under the room (y1) and the walls are not mine; the room's light and lane were checked only against the bare air box.
elements.md has no item specific to the cottage bedroom, so no checkbox was ticked in plan.md or elements.md.

waste.what: Worked out each furniture cell by hand from the plan grid and wrote the three y-layers of layers() rows separately (floor, table top, candle, lantern rows), with the row and column offsets counted by eye.
waste.cost: About 6 layers() calls and 4 coordinate checks by hand; one wrong offset (lantern row) found only by the room check.
waste.tool: A `mcd plan --draw` option that takes a furniture spec (name, cell, facing) and emits the layers() text, or a layers() variant that takes a sparse list of [x,y,z,block,state] cells.

waste.what: Table built by hand as dark_oak_fence plus a top slab on the fence, and chairs as stairs facing the table, all placed in legend strings with the facings worked out per cell.
waste.cost: About 3 retries on which stair facing reads as back-to-wall; no separate build helper.
waste.tool: A furniture helper in vocab: table(g, x, z, {top:'fence'}) and chair(g, x, z, facingToTable) that set the fence, top slab and stairs states together.

waste.what: The room check can only give a walk verdict once the whole shell exists, so I could not verify the lane in this copy and had to check the lane by reading the floor grid.
waste.cost: One check run that reported UNREACHABLE for reasons outside my part, then a manual lane trace from the door cell to the bed and chest.
waste.tool: `mcd room --assume-entry x,y,z` so a single room can be walk-checked from its doorway without the rest of the building.

companions.task: Check the two hanging lanterns and the candle against the final ceiling once the cottage plate exists, and confirm the room stays at light 8+ with the shell in place.
Make the table and chairs as a set, with the chest and nightstand matched in wood, instead of a fence post and a top slab assembled from a legend string.
